result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the specific problem behaviors and propose autosave, removing the unit-change confirmation, safer reset handling, and checks after release. B goes further: new hives copy settings from an existing hive, an Essentials/Advanced split separates common from rare settings without removing any, and a settings-only reset can be undone. A is tighter and handles the risks well, but it lacks copy-from-hive and is less explicit about demoting rarely used settings. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers handle the save model, the unit-change confirmation and the reset button well, and both name the specific problem behaviors. A covers more of the rubric: new hives copy settings from an existing hive, settings move into Essentials and Advanced groups without removing any, and reset gets undo and scoped options. B gives sharper post-release metrics and a clearer staged rollout, but lacks copy-from-existing-hive and never says outright that no options are removed.
